user.title: Decision model
user.description: Pick which model decides every command and query. The hosted TypeSafe API (Jev) needs an API key from {console_url}. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works too - a self-hosted Clef, Von, Laya, or a plain LLM served by vLLM, llama.cpp or Ollama.

data_description.decision_backend: TypeSafe hosts Jev as a paid API. OpenAI-compatible covers every self-hosted decision model: Clef, Von, Laya, or a plain LLM behind vLLM, llama.cpp or Ollama.

llm.title: Language model (optional)
llm.description: The decision model handles every command and query on its own. A language model is only used to split requests that contain several commands, and to answer general questions. Leave this blank to skip it.

data_description.model: Jev is the only hosted model today; jev-latest follows releases.

data_description.decision_base_url: Root of the endpoint, without /v1 - for example http://homeassistant.local:8000 or http://192.168.1.50:11434. /v1/chat/completions is appended automatically.
data_description.decision_api_key: Only if the endpoint needs one. Local servers usually do not.
data_description.decision_timeout: Seconds to wait for one decision. Self-hosted models on modest hardware need more than the hosted API.
data_description.model: Model name as the endpoint reports it - for example clef-flash, von or qwen3.5-9b.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the decision backend.

data.name: Name
data.always_confirm_risky: Always confirm before unlocking or opening
data.inline_entity_descriptions: Describe every entity inside the question
data.bypass_local_intents: Handle every command, including ones Home Assistant recognises
data.llm_control_devices: Let the language model control devices

data_description.always_confirm_risky: Ask first before unlocking a door, opening a garage or disarming an alarm, however sure the model is. Turning this off lets confident requests through silently.
data_description.inline_entity_descriptions: Costs roughly twice the tokens. Only worth turning on if the agent picks the wrong device.
data_description.bypass_local_intents: By default Home Assistant's own sentence matcher keeps the phrasings it recognises, and only sends the rest here. Turn this on to send everything here instead.
data_description.system_prompt: Extra instructions for general-knowledge answers - a persona, a language rule, how brief to be. Appended after the built-in safety rules, so it cannot make the assistant claim to have controlled a device. Only used when a language model is configured.
data_description.llm_control_devices: When the decision model is unsure, the language model may act on the devices exposed to Assist through Home Assistant's tool API - same permissions as the built-in LLM agents. Off by default; without it the language model can only answer in text.
